_doc: Hand-authored dependency direction for the Atlas frameworks landscape, not publisher containment and not derived from crosswalk data. Every framework-pair edge in the canonical graph is relationship_class "correlation" or "applicability" — docs/DATA_POLICY.md is explicit that these classes cannot supply parent, ancestors, structural level, or depth. Confirmed directly against data/generated/atlas-network.json: NIST Zero Trust's own edge to both SP 800-53 and CSF 2.0 carries both "supports" and "supported_by" in the same aggregated bucket, so relationship_type cannot mechanically supply direction either. `parentCatalogId` here is an editorial call about which framework a reader should understand as depending on which, reviewed with the product owner (2026-09-04). It drives layout position only — it must never be presented as, or merged into, a published crosswalk. Any framework-pair edge in the canonical graph that does not match a catalog's declared parent here renders as a secondary cross-link, not a tree position.

roots.rationale: The dataset's hub — twelve other frameworks select from, assess, correlate to, or baseline it, and it depends on nothing else here.
Adversary technique taxonomy. D3FEND is MITRE's declared countermeasure-to-ATT&CK mapping, not the reverse.

Used independently in practice — practitioners orient from CSF's functions and drill into 800-53 for control detail, not the reverse, even though the raw crosswalk data's own edge runs 800-53 -> CSF. Confirmed with product owner 2026-09-04.
A governmentwide information-handling policy (32 CFR Part 2002), independent of the 800-53 control catalog. Every edge it has is inbound (things that protect CUI reference it), never outbound.

RMF. Used independently in practice, the same as CSF, even though it technically references 800-53/800-53B/FIPS-199/FIPS-200 as steps in its process. Confirmed with product owner 2026-09-04 — RMF and CSF are each their own door, not a child of 800-53.

dod-zt.rationale: DoD Zero Trust's pillars select controls from SP 800-53.

nist-zt.rationale: NIST Zero Trust selects SP 800-53 controls (1,114 shared records vs. 632 for its smaller CSF relationship, which renders as a secondary line).

fedramp-rev5.rationale: FedRAMP Rev. 5 baselines are literally SP 800-53 control selections.

nist-800-53a.rationale: The assessment-procedures companion volume to 800-53 — exists to assess 800-53 controls.

nist-800-53b.rationale: The Low/Moderate/High control-baseline companion volume to 800-53.

nist-iot-cybersecurity.rationale: Maps its device requirements to SP 800-53 controls.

fips-200.rationale: Judgment call: FIPS 200 predates and informed 800-53's development, so an argument exists the other way. Kept as a child of the dataset's hub for simplicity; its only real edge is directly to 800-53.

disa-cci.rationale: CCIs exist specifically to correlate 800-53 control statements to assessable, implementable items.

fips-199.rationale: Impact categorization feeds directly into which 800-53B baseline (Low/Moderate/High) applies — its only real edge is to 800-53B, not to 800-53 or RMF directly.

disa-stig.rationale: STIGs implement via CCI correlation (25,771 shared records, the dataset's heaviest relationship).

disa-srg.rationale: SRGs implement via CCI correlation, the same as STIGs.

mitre-d3fend.rationale: MITRE's declared countermeasure-to-ATT&CK mapping. Its smaller direct edge to SP 800-53 renders as a secondary cross-link.

mitre-attack-ics.rationale: MITRE's ICS-specific extension of the main ATT&CK Enterprise framework, not a thing D3FEND references. Its own edge to D3FEND renders as a secondary line between two children of the same root.

nist-800-171-rev2.rationale: Exists specifically to protect CUI per the program policy.

nist-800-172.rationale: Enhanced CUI protection requirements — same grounding as 800-171-rev2. Its edge from CMMC 2.0 renders as a secondary line.

nist-800-171.rationale: Rev. 3 of the same CUI-protection standard as 800-171-rev2 — kept consistent with its sibling revision rather than split across two different primary parents. Its larger data relationships to SP 800-53 (157 records) and CSF (313 records) render as secondary lines.

cmmc-2.rationale: CMMC 2.0's foundational level incorporates 800-171-rev2; its edge to 800-172 (its higher maturity level) renders as a secondary line.

_unconnectedDoc: Catalogs with zero frameworks-level edges in the canonical graph as of 2026-09-04 get no entry here. They stay in the Atlas's existing honest 'no crosswalks mapped yet' treatment rather than being forced into the tree.
